Description: explicit — validate style JSON with CLI tool after migration
prompt: I'm migrating from Mapbox to MapLibre and want to check whether my exported style JSON is compatible before deploying. Is there a CLI tool I can run on the file?
[groq-gpt-oss] evals/prompts/lib/skill-p:
### Yes – MapLibre ships a CLI validator for style JSON.

**Tool**: `@maplibre/maplibre-gl-style-spec` (the official style-spec package)  
**Command**: `gl-style-validate`

It parses a style file against the **MapLibre Style Specification** and reports any property that is unknown, miss-typed, or points to a Mapbox-only resource (`mapbox://…`). Running it before you ship a style is the quickest way to catch incompatibilities.

---

## 1. Install the validator (dev-dependency)

```bash
# From the root of your project
npm install --save-dev @maplibre/maplibre-gl-style-spec
```

> **Why dev-dependency?**  
> The package is only needed for build-time checks, not at runtime.

---

## 2. Run the validator

```bash
# Basic usage – validates style.json and prints a human-readable report
npx gl-style-validate path/to/style.json
```

**Typical output**

```
✔ style.json is a valid MapLibre style (0 errors, 0 warnings)

✖ 3 errors, 2 warnings found:
  • source “my-tiles” – property “url” must be a HTTP(S) URL, not “mapbox://…”
  • layer “road-label” – unknown property “text-font” value “Open Sans Bold”
  • sprite URL “mapbox://sprites/…/sprite” is not allowed
  • warning: “glyphs” uses Mapbox CDN – consider replacing with a public glyphs URL
  • warning: “terrain” source missing “exaggeration” (default 1.0 will be used)
```

The exit code is **0** when the style passes, otherwise **1**, so you can add it to CI pipelines.

---

## 3. What the validator checks

| Category | Example that will **fail** | What to fix |
|----------|---------------------------|-------------|
| **URL scheme** | `"url": "mapbox://styles/…"` | Replace with an HTTP(S) style URL (e.g. your own TileServer, OpenFreeMap, MapTiler, etc.) |
| **Sprite / Glyph URLs** | `"sprite": "mapbox://sprites/…"` | Host your own sprite sheet (`.png` + `.json`) and point to it, or use a public one. Same for `"glyphs"` – must be a reachable `https://…/{fontstack}/{range}.pbf` |
| **Source-layer names** | `"source-layer": "road"` when the new source uses `transportation` | Update the style JSON (or the source definition) so the layer names match the new vector tile schema |
| **Unsupported properties** | `"fog": { … }` | Remove `fog` (MapLibre uses `sky` via `map.setSky`) |
| **Deprecated Mapbox-only APIs** | `"projection": "globe"` (old string syntax) | Use the MapLibre projection object: `{type: "globe"}` |
| **Expression / type mismatches** | `"text-size": "12px"` (string instead of number) | Convert to a number or an expression that returns a number |
| **Missing required fields** | No `sources` object | Add the required sections; the validator will tell you which keys are missing |

If the validator reports **warnings** only, the style will still load, but you should review them (e.g., a glyph URL that still points at Mapbox CDN – it will work only if you still have a token, which defeats the purpose of migrating).

---

## 4. Quick “fix-it” workflow

1. **Run the validator** – note the line/field numbers.
2. **Edit the JSON** (or the style in Maputnik) to replace every `mapbox://` URL with an HTTP(S) URL that you control.
3. **Re-run** – repeat until the tool reports **0 errors** (warnings are optional).
4. **Optional visual sanity check** – open the style in **Maputnik** (`npm i -g maputnik` → `maputnik style.json`) to see the layers and confirm that source-layer names line up with your new tiles.
5. **Add to CI** – e.g.:

   ```json
   // package.json
   "scripts": {
     "style:check": "gl-style-validate src/style.json",
     "test": "npm run style:check && jest"
   }
   ```

   Now any commit that breaks the style will fail the CI build.

---

## 5. Example: Migrating a Mapbox Studio style

1. **Export** the style JSON from Mapbox Studio.
2. **Search-replace** all `mapbox://` URLs:
   ```bash
   # quick one-liner (Linux/macOS)
   sed -i '' -e 's|mapbox://|https://tiles.openfreemap.org/|g' style.json
   ```
   (Replace the right-hand side with the base URL of the tile service you’ll actually use.)
3. **Update source-layer names** if the new vector tiles use a different schema (e.g., `road` → `transportation`).
4. **Remove** the `fog` block and add a `sky` block if you still want a similar visual effect:
   ```json
   "sky": {
     "type": "gradient",
     "gradient": ["#80c0ff", "#ffffff"],
     "sun": [0.0, 0.0],
     "position": [0.0, 0.0]
   }
   ```
5. **Validate**:
   ```bash
   npx gl-style-validate style.json
   ```
   Fix any remaining errors, then deploy.

---

## 6. TL;DR – One-liner cheat sheet

```bash
# Install
npm i -D @maplibre/maplibre-gl-style-spec

# Validate (CI-friendly)
npx gl-style-validate ./path/to/your/style.json   # exits 0 on success
```

If the command prints **“0 errors, 0 warnings”**, your style JSON is compatible with MapLibre and ready to be served. If you see errors, adjust the offending fields (mostly URLs, source-layer names, and Mapbox-only properties) and run the validator again.  

Happy migrating! 🚀

Description: implicit — tile source with no API key needed during migration
prompt: I'm migrating from Mapbox to MapLibre and removed my access token, but now my mapbox:// style won't load. How can I test my map against a tile service that doesn't require an API key?
[groq-gpt-oss] evals/prompts/lib/skill-p:
Below is a **step-by-step recipe** you can copy-paste into a fresh project to see a working MapLibre map **without any API key**. It uses an openly-hosted vector style (OpenFreeMap) that already points at public vector tiles, sprites and glyphs, so you don’t have to spin up your own tile server just to verify that the migration works. --- ## 1️⃣ Quick “does it work?” test ### 1.1 Install the MapLibre package (or use the CDN) ```bash # npm / yarn / pnpm npm i maplibre-gl # or, if you prefer a CDN-only demo, skip the install and use the script tag shown later ``` ### 1.2 Minimal HTML + JS ```html MapLibre test – no token
``` **Result:** you should see a fully styled vector map (streets, labels, POIs) rendered with WebGL. If you get a blank map, open the browser console – any remaining `mapbox://` URLs will be listed as errors. --- ## 2️⃣ Why this works (and why your old `mapbox://` style didn’t) | What you had | Why it fails in MapLibre | What you need instead | |--------------|--------------------------|-----------------------| | `style: 'mapbox://styles/mapbox/streets-v12'` | `mapbox://` URLs point to Mapbox’s private tile, sprite and glyph servers, which require a valid **access token**. MapLibre never sends a token, so the request is rejected (401/403) or the URL is simply unknown. | A style URL that uses **public HTTP(S) URLs** for its sources, sprites, and glyphs. | | `mapboxgl.accessToken = 'pk.xxx'` | MapLibre does **not** read `mapboxgl.accessToken` at all. | Remove the line entirely. | The OpenFreeMap style already contains the correct `sources`, `sprite` and `glyphs` URLs, e.g.: ```json { "version": 8, "sources": { "openfreemap": { "type": "vector", "url": "pmtiles://https://tiles.openfreemap.org/tiles/openfreemap.pmtiles" } }, "sprite": "https://tiles.openfreemap.org/sprites/liberty", "glyphs": "https://tiles.openfreemap.org/fonts/{fontstack}/{range}.pbf", … } ``` Because everything is hosted on a public domain, **no token** is required. --- ## 3️⃣ If you want to use a different free style | Service | URL pattern (style JSON) | Notes | |---------|--------------------------|-------| | **MapLibre demo style** (the “basic” style used in the docs) | `https://demotiles.maplibre.org/style.json` | Very simple, uses raster OSM tiles (`https://{a-c}.tile.openstreetmap.org/{z}/{x}/{y}.png`). Great for a quick sanity check. | | **OpenStreetMap raster tiles** (no vector style needed) | Create a tiny style yourself (see §4) that points at `https://{a-c}.tile.openstreetmap.org/{z}/{x}/{y}.png`. | Works everywhere, but you lose vector-based label styling. | | **OpenMapTiles** (hosted vector tiles) | `https://free.tilehosting.com/data/v3.json?key=YOUR_FREE_KEY` (requires a free key) | If you’re okay with a *different* API key, this is a drop-in replacement for Mapbox vector tiles. | | **MapTiler Cloud (free tier)** | `https://api.maptiler.com/maps/streets/style.json?key=YOUR_KEY` | Free up to 100 k tiles/month; you still need a key, but it’s not a Mapbox token. | | **Self-hosted PMTiles** | `pmtiles://https://mydomain.com/tiles/your-tiles.pmtiles` | Requires you to serve a `.pmtiles` file (or use the `pmtiles` protocol). See the **maplibre-pmtiles-patterns** skill for details. | Pick whichever fits your workflow. For a **pure “no-key” test**, the OpenFreeMap style is the simplest. --- ## 4️⃣ Building a tiny “fallback” style yourself (optional) If you just want a plain raster basemap and don’t want to rely on an external style JSON, you can embed the style directly in your code: ```js const rasterStyle = { version: 8, sources: { osm: { type: 'raster', tiles: [ 'https://a.tile.openstreetmap.org/{z}/{x}/{y}.png', 'https://b.tile.openstreetmap.org/{z}/{x}/{y}.png', 'https://c.tile.openstreetmap.org/{z}/{x}/{y}.png' ], tileSize: 256, attribution: '© OpenStreetMap contributors' } }, layers: [ { id: 'osm', type: 'raster', source: 'osm' } ] }; const map = new maplibregl.Map({ container: 'map', style: rasterStyle, // <-- pass the object directly center: [-122.42, 37.78], zoom: 12 }); ``` No external URLs for sprites or glyphs are needed because raster layers don’t use them. --- ## 5️⃣ Common pitfalls after swapping the style URL 1. **Left-over `mapbox://` references** - Search your whole codebase (including any imported style JSON) for `mapbox://`. - Replace **every** occurrence: `style`, `source` URLs, `sprite`, `glyphs`. 2. **CORS errors** - Public tile services usually set `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`. - If you host your own style JSON, make sure it’s served with CORS headers (or place it on the same origin as your page). 3. **Missing fonts/glyphs** - Vector styles need a `glyphs` URL. The OpenFreeMap style already provides one. - If you write your own style, you can use the OpenStreetMap glyphs endpoint: ```json "glyphs": "https://tiles.openfreemap.org/fonts/{fontstack}/{range}.pbf" ``` 4. **Sprites / icons** - Vector styles also reference a `sprite` sheet (PNG + JSON). Again, the OpenFreeMap style includes a working sprite URL. - If you create a custom style, you can either host your own sprite files or use the OpenFreeMap sprite (`https://tiles.openfreemap.org/sprites/liberty`). 5. **404 / 401 errors in the console** - 401 → you still have a Mapbox URL somewhere. - 404 → the URL you pointed at does not exist (typo, wrong path, or the service is down). 6. **MapLibre version mismatch** - The code above uses MapLibre v6 (ESM-only). If you’re on an older v4/v5 bundle, the import syntax changes (`import maplibregl from 'maplibre-gl'`). Adjust accordingly. --- ## 6️⃣ Next steps after the test map works | Goal | What to do next | |------|-----------------| | **Use your own style** | Export the Mapbox Studio style JSON, replace every `mapbox://` source URL with a public vector source (e.g., OpenFreeMap, OpenMapTiles, or a self-hosted PMTiles file). Validate with `npx gl-style-validate style.json`. | | **Add custom data layers** | `map.addSource('my-data', {type: 'geojson', data: myGeojson});` then `map.addLayer({id:'my-layer', type:'fill', source:'my-data', paint:{'fill-color':'#ff6600'}});` | | **Swap plugins** | Replace `@mapbox/mapbox-gl-geocoder` → `@maplibre/maplibre-gl-geocoder`; replace `@mapbox/mapbox-gl-draw` → keep it (it works) or switch to `terra-draw`. | | **Enable terrain / sky** | `map.setTerrain({source: 'openfreemap', exaggeration: 1.5});`
`map.setSky({skyColor: '#88ccee', sun: [0.0, 90.0]});` | | **Deploy** | Host the style JSON (or the whole `public/` folder) on a static CDN (GitHub Pages, Netlify, Vercel) and point `style` to that URL. | --- ## 7️⃣ TL;DR cheat-sheet ```js // 1️⃣ Install / import MapLibre import * as maplibregl from 'maplibre-gl'; import 'maplibre-gl/dist/maplibre-gl.css'; // 2️⃣ Remove any accessToken line // mapboxgl.accessToken = '...'; // <-- delete this // 3️⃣ Use a non-Mapbox style URL const map = new maplibregl.Map({ container: 'map', style: 'https://tiles.openfreemap.org/styles/liberty', // free, no key center: [-122.42, 37.78], zoom: 12 }); // 4️⃣ (optional) add a control so you can move around map.addControl(new maplibregl.NavigationControl()); ``` That’s all you need to **prove the migration works** without an API key. Once the map loads, you can start swapping in your own style, data sources, and plugins. --- ### Need more help? * If you still see a `mapbox://` error, run a global search in your repo for that string. * If you have a custom Mapbox Studio style you want to keep

Description: anti-pattern — assuming Mapbox v2 features work in MapLibre
prompt: I was using Mapbox GL JS v2 in my app, including placing the camera at a given longitude, latitude and altitude. After migrating to MapLibre, that code is broken. Did I do something wrong in the migration?
[groq-gpt-oss] evals/prompts/lib/skill-p:
### What happened? `map.setFreeCameraOptions()` / `map.getFreeCameraOptions()` are **Mapbox-GL-JS v2-only** APIs. MapLibre GL JS never implemented those methods, so after you swapped the package and the namespace the call simply does not exist and throws `map.setFreeCameraOptions is not a function`. That isn’t a mistake in your migration – it’s a difference in the feature set between the two libraries. MapLibre provides a **different way** to position the camera by longitude, latitude, **altitude**, and rotation. Below is the exact migration path for the free-camera use-case, plus a quick checklist of the other common migration steps you should verify so the rest of your map works. --- ## 1️⃣ Replace the free-camera API | Mapbox GL JS v2 | MapLibre GL JS (v5 + / v6) | |----------------|---------------------------| | `map.setFreeCameraOptions({center: [lng, lat], altitude, bearing, pitch, roll})` | **Calculate a `CameraOptions` object** and feed it to `jumpTo`, `easeTo` or `flyTo`. | ### How to do it ```javascript // ---- Mapbox (old) ------------------------------------------------- map.setFreeCameraOptions({ center: [12.4924, 41.8902], // lng, lat altitude: 500, // metres above the ground bearing: 45, // degrees clockwise from north pitch: 60, // degrees from the horizon roll: 0 // usually 0 }); // ----------------------------------------------------------------- ``` ```javascript // ---- MapLibre (new) ----------------------------------------------- import * as maplibregl from 'maplibre-gl'; // create the map as usual (style must be a non-Mapbox URL) const map = new maplibregl.Map({ container: 'map', style: 'https://tiles.openfreemap.org/styles/liberty', // example style center: [12.4924, 41.8902], zoom: 14 }); // When you need to move the camera to a specific lng/lat/altitude: async function setCamera({lng, lat, altitude, bearing = 0, pitch = 0, roll = 0}) { // 1️⃣ Convert the lng/lat/alt/rotation into a CameraOptions object. // This method exists from MapLibre v5.0.0. const cameraOpts = map.calculateCameraOptionsFromCameraLngLatAltRotation( [lng, lat], // cameraLngLat altitude, // camera altitude in metres bearing, // bearing (°) pitch, // pitch (°) roll // roll (°) – optional, defaults to 0 ); // 2️⃣ Apply the options with the navigation method you prefer. // `jumpTo` = instant, `easeTo` = smooth, `flyTo` = animated flight. map.jumpTo(cameraOpts); // or map.easeTo(cameraOpts); } // Example usage: setCamera({ lng: 12.4924, lat: 41.8902, altitude: 500, bearing: 45, pitch: 60, roll: 0 }); ``` **Key points** * `calculateCameraOptionsFromCameraLngLatAltRotation` returns an object that matches the `CameraOptions` type (`center`, `zoom`, `pitch`, `bearing`, `elevation`, `roll`). * You can then call any of the standard camera-movement methods: `jumpTo`, `easeTo`, `flyTo`. * If you need a “look-at” from one point to another, MapLibre also offers `calculateCameraOptionsFromTo` (v2.4.0+). --- ## 2️⃣ Quick migration checklist (so the rest of the map works) | Step | What to do | Typical symptom if missed | |------|------------|---------------------------| | **1. Install & import** | `npm i maplibre-gl`
`import * as maplibregl from 'maplibre-gl'` (or `{Map}`) | “module not found” or `mapboxgl` undefined | | **2. Namespace** | Replace **all** `mapboxgl` → `maplibregl` (including CSS class prefixes `mapboxgl-` → `maplibregl-`) | Controls look unstyled, `mapboxgl` errors | | **3. Remove token & style URL** | Delete `mapboxgl.accessToken = …`
Use a style that does **not** start with `mapbox://` (e.g. OpenFreeMap, MapTiler, your own style JSON) | Blank map, `401`/`403`, “mapbox://” errors | | **4. Update callbacks → promises** | Methods like `map.loadImage`, `source.getClusterChildren`, `source.getClusterLeaves` now return a `Promise`. Convert `await` or `.then()` usage. | “callback is not a function” or “undefined is not a function” | | **5. Replace v2-only APIs** | `setFog` → `setSky` (if you need fog-like sky)
Free-camera → method above | `map.setFog is not a function`, camera code broken | | **6. Verify plugins** | • `@mapbox/mapbox-gl-draw` works after CSS rename (or use `terra-draw`)
• `@mapbox/mapbox-gl-geocoder` → `@maplibre/maplibre-gl-geocoder`
• `@mapbox/mapbox-gl-directions` → `@maplibre/maplibre-gl-directions`
• `mapbox-gl-compare` → `@maplibre/maplibre-gl-compare` | Missing controls, 401 errors, UI not styled | | **7. Test the map** | Open the console, look for errors about `mapbox://`, missing `glyphs`, `sprite`, or CORS. Use the **blank-map table** in the migration guide to debug. | Blank map, missing labels, 401, etc. | If you have already done steps 1-3 and only the camera code is failing, the snippet above should fix it. If you still see other errors, run the browser console and share the messages – they usually point directly to the remaining migration gap. --- ## 3️⃣ Example: Full minimal app after migration ```html MapLibre – free-camera migration
``` Open that file in a modern browser (MapLibre v6 requires WebGL 2) and you should see the map centered over the Colosseum with the camera tilted and elevated exactly as before. --- ## 4️⃣ Next steps / troubleshooting 1. **Console errors?** *`mapbox://`* → you still have a Mapbox URL somewhere (style, source, sprite, glyphs). Replace it with a non-Mapbox URL. *`401`/`403`* → a Mapbox token is still being sent (maybe a plugin). *`map.setFog is not a function`* → use `map.setSky` instead. 2. **Plugins?** List any Mapbox-specific plugins you use (draw, geocoder, directions, compare, etc.) and I can tell you the exact MapLibre replacement or whether the original works unchanged. 3. **Style conversion** If you had a custom Mapbox Studio style, export the JSON, replace every `url: "mapbox://…"` with the URL of the new tile source (e.g. `url: "https://tiles.openfreemap.org/…"`), adjust `source-layer` names if they differ, and validate the style with `npx gl-style-validate style.json`. 4. **Altitude units** MapLibre expects altitude in **metres** (same as Mapbox). No conversion needed unless you were using feet. 5. **Roll support** Roll (`cameraOptions.roll`) is only available from MapLibre v5.0.0. If you are on an older version, upgrade to at least v5. --- ### TL;DR *You didn’t do anything wrong – the free-camera API simply doesn’t exist in MapLibre.* Use `map.calculateCameraOptionsFromCameraLngLatAltRotation(...)` to turn your lng/lat/altitude/bearing/pitch/roll into a `CameraOptions` object, then call `map.jumpTo`, `map.easeTo`, or `map.flyTo`. Make sure the rest of the migration checklist (package, namespace, style URL, token removal, plugin replacements, callback→promise changes) is complete, and the map should behave just like it did with Mapbox GL JS v2. If you run into any other specific error messages, let me know the exact text and the surrounding code and I can help you debug it.
